methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort of 659 patients with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria, appropriate outcome definitions (PFS, OS), and correct statistical methods (Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression). AI classifier validated with F1 score 0.81. Sensitivity analyses on cut-off values and subgroup stratification by histology and MMR status strengthen rigor. Single-center design and lack of external validation are acknowledged limitations but do not undermine the internal validity of this cohort analysis.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual retrospective cohort study demonstrating that AI-quantified TILs significantly predict progression-free survival (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.43–0.87, p<0.01) and overall survival (HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.33–0.86, p=0.01) in endometrial carcinoma. Direct prognostic biomarker application with clear path to clinical practice for patient risk stratification. Finding that high TILs correlate with better outcomes and MMR deficiency status addresses an unmet need in EC prognostic assessment.

reporting_quality.justification: Study adheres closely to REMARK standards for prognostic biomarker reporting: clear population definition (n=659, 1989-2022), histopathological methods detailed, outcomes precisely defined, statistical analysis fully described with multivariable modeling, and limitations transparently acknowledged including single-center design and lack of external validation. However, no statement regarding data availability or deposit in a recognized repository; methods are reproducible in principle but raw data and trained AI classifier not made publicly accessible.

novelty_literature.justification: Applies established deep learning methodology (Object Phenotyper for automated lymphocyte detection) to a novel application domain—quantifying TILs around the invasive frontline of endometrial carcinoma. While TILs have been recognized as prognostic markers in EC through manual assessment, the systematic AI-based quantification in this specific anatomical region and validation of prognostic utility represents a meaningful methodological extension. This is not first-in-class AI-TIL work (prior reports in ovarian, esophageal, and colorectal malignancies cited) but fills a documented gap specific to EC.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is clearly written with logical flow from introduction through results and discussion. Methods section is comprehensive and reproducible; figures effectively communicate the AI-detected structures (Figure 2) and survival outcomes (Figure 5). Tables present baseline characteristics and multivariate hazard ratios with appropriate confidence intervals. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within prior literature and identifies specific limitations (single-center, small training set, lack of POLE evaluation). Minor areas for tightening exist but overall publication-ready in presentation.

key_strengths: Rigorous AI-based quantification of TILs with validated classifier (F1 0.81) applied to large cohort (n=659) with long follow-up (median 63 months)
Strong prognostic signals for both PFS and OS with appropriate multivariable adjustment and meaningful subgroup analyses stratified by histological type and MMR status
Transparent acknowledgment of limitations (single-center, no external validation, small training set) and clear roadmap for future work
Clear clinical relevance for endometrial carcinoma prognostication and alignment with MMR-immune status biology
key_concerns: Lack of external validation from independent institution(s) limits generalizability and confidence in model reproducibility
No data availability or code sharing statement; trained AI classifier and patient-level data not deposited in recognized repositories, hindering reproducibility
Small training set (2,235 lymphocytes from 4 cases) for AI classifier may limit model robustness and generalization to diverse histological subtypes and tissue preparation protocols
Absence of POLE mutation assessment despite authors acknowledging documented interaction with TILs and MMR status; limits mechanistic completeness
Manual annotation of invasive frontline without inter-observer reproducibility assessment introduces potential source of inconsistency
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent, methodologically sound retrospective prognostic biomarker study with clear clinical relevance and appropriate statistical analysis. Single-center design, lack of external validation, and missing data/code availability preclude Tier 2 consideration. Suitable for Tier 3 (4–9.9 JIF) journals (e.g., Cancers, Frontiers in Oncology) with minor revisions to address data sharing and prospective/multi-center validation plans.
